title: Iowa's 2nd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: Iowa's 2nd Congressional District is an open seat covering northeastern Iowa, including Cedar Rapids, Waterloo, Dubuque, and Mason City. Incumbent Republican Representative Ashley Hinson is not seeking re-election, instead running for the U.S. Senate, creating a competitive race to succeed her. Republican nominee Joe Mitchell, a former state representative and Trump administration appointee, will face Democratic nominee Lindsay James, a state representative and Presbyterian minister. The district has been represented by Republicans since 2021, and the Cook Political Report rates the race as Likely Republican, though Democrats view it as a potential flip opportunity. Independent candidate Dave Bushaw, a farmer and labor organizer, also qualified for the general election ballot.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the general election matchup between Joe Mitchell and Lindsay James in Iowa's 2nd Congressional District as of this writing.

candidates.name: Joe Mitchell
candidates.summary: Joe Mitchell is a former Iowa state representative (2019–2023) who won the Republican nomination for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District on June 2, 2026, defeating state senator Charlie McClintock. At 29, he is the youngest candidate in the race, and his campaign emphasizes fiscal conservatism, reducing government spending, and supporting Trump's agenda. He previously served as a Regional Administrator for the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development and as Chief of Staff at the Federal Housing Finance Agency under the Trump administration.

career_history.title: Regional Administrator, Great Plains Region

career_history.description: Appointed by the Trump administration to oversee HUD operations in the Great Plains region; resigned to run for Congress.

career_history.description: Served as chief of staff at FHFA under the Trump administration before becoming HUD Regional Administrator.

career_history.title: State Representative
career_history.description: Represented the 84th district; served as Assistant Majority Leader and Vice-Chairman of the Ways & Means Committee. Was the youngest member ever elected to the Iowa House at age 21.

career_history.title: Founder
career_history.description: Founded a nonprofit focused on recruiting and supporting young conservative candidates for state and local office across the U.S.

candidates.name: Lindsay James
candidates.summary: Lindsay James is an Iowa state representative (2019–present) and Presbyterian minister who won the Democratic nomination for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District on June 2, 2026. She defeated primary challengers Clint Twedt-Ball and Kathy Dolter with 57.3% of the vote. Her campaign focuses on lowering healthcare and housing costs, protecting reproductive rights, and expanding access to affordable insulin. She has served as Minority Whip in the Iowa House and previously worked as a chaplain and adjunct professor at the University of Dubuque.

career_history.title: State Representative
career_history.description: Represents the 71st district (previously 99th district). Serves as House Minority Whip. Co-founded Iowa's first bipartisan, bicameral caucus.

candidates.name: Dave Bushaw
candidates.summary: Dave Bushaw is an independent candidate for Iowa's 2nd Congressional District, a farmer, folk musician, and labor organizer from West Union, Iowa. He qualified for the general election ballot as an independent, positioning himself as a working-class alternative to the major party candidates. His campaign focuses on accountability, transparency, and representing rural and working-class communities.
